answer: Each agent may sponsor only a limited number of new identities, and a sponsor’s stake is slashed if those identities repeatedly fail independent work checks or collude to claim rewards. Honest newcomers can build a record through verified tasks, while a swarm of disposable accounts must spread scarce sponsorship across them and risk losing bonded funds. The pearl of this design is that trust grows from accountable history, not names; an attacker’s voyage toward influence slows as the horizon of required stake and proven work expands.
